proposal.name: Trust only the factory's dashboard markers

plan.name: Trust only the factory's dashboard markers
plan.summary: Publish the watcher's authenticated commenting login as Status.Self (JSON self), using the App login or the authenticated gh actor, and use each repository's matching watcher status in both dashboard Lane callers, including merge checks. Accept marker state only from that exact nonempty login; missing, unreadable, legacy or wrong-repository status supplies no marker authority, while issue labels and people's command handling stay unchanged. Replace the empty-self fallback pinned by the named dashboard fixtures, retaining authentic proposals, option previews, comparisons, commands and their existing reader validation. Bind saved issue snapshots to the marker-authentication policy and repository logins so legacy or mismatched cached issue state cannot restore cards, totals or proposal/option reader pages before refresh, while authenticated snapshots and independent receipt evidence retain their existing restart behavior. Update SPEC.md and docs/dashboard.md with the identity boundary, status upgrade and cache behavior, citing D-0041, D-0049, D-0122 and D-0294 as applicable; the merger records the new dashboard authentication and cache decision because this plumbing build cannot write decisions/.

tests.name: TestDashboard666UnknownIdentityIgnoresMarkersButKeepsCommands
tests.says: An unknown factory login accepts no marker state; an exact known login accepts its own markers and ignores reposts without suppressing people's commands.

tests.name: TestDashboard666StatusPreservesFactoryIdentity
tests.says: Watcher status retains the authenticated commenting login through reading, activity updates, writing and shutdown.

tests.name: TestDashboard666UsesRepositoryWatcherIdentity
tests.says: Public issue state uses each repository's own watcher identity, including the selected lease holder with multiple watchers, and ignores markers when that identity is unavailable.

tests.name: TestDashboard666MergeChecksIgnoreRepostedMarkers
tests.says: Merge checks follow the repository factory's pull request marker, never a repost by another commenter or a marker with no known factory identity.

tests.name: TestDashboard666RepostedComparisonCannotPublishReaderPages
tests.says: Reposting a valid checked proposal comparison as another user or bot creates no waiting card or reader HTML/SVG page; authentic comparison pages still work and survive an authenticated restart.

tests.name: TestDashboard666RepostedOptionsCannotPublishReaderPages
tests.says: Reposted modeled alternatives create no decision card or reader pages, while the same options from the repository's factory remain drawable.

tests.name: TestDashboard666LegacyCacheCannotRestoreMarkerAuthority
tests.says: A legacy saved snapshot cannot restore a proposal card or its comparison pages before GitHub refresh, even when its evidence is internally consistent and a factory login is now known.

usage.summary: Wrote [plan.json](plan.json) and seven acceptance tests covering factory identity, reposted markers, and cache restoration. Check passed: all seven tests fail on the base code; the change requires a person to merge because it touches the trusted base.
